title: चतुर्नवतितमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Parashurama tells of King Dambhodbhava, who in his pride sought an equal in battle and was directed to the sages Nara and Narayana. Nara defeated his whole army with blades of grass, and the humbled king learned to honour Brahmins; Parashurama warns that Arjuna and Krishna are Nara and Narayana, and urges Duryodhana to make peace.
summary.kn: ಗರ್ವದಿಂದ ಯುದ್ಧದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮಾನನನ್ನು ಹುಡುಕಿ ನರನಾರಾಯಣ ಋಷಿಗಳ ಬಳಿಗೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟ ದಂಭೋದ್ಭವ ರಾಜನ ಕಥೆಯನ್ನು ಪರಶುರಾಮನು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ನರನು ದರ್ಭೆಯ ಕಡ್ಡಿಗಳಿಂದಲೇ ಅವನ ಇಡೀ ಸೈನ್ಯವನ್ನು ಸೋಲಿಸಿದನು, ವಿನಯಗೊಂಡ ರಾಜನು ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರನ್ನು ಗೌರವಿಸಲು ಕಲಿತನು; ಅರ್ಜುನ ಶ್ರೀಕೃಷ್ಣರೇ ನರನಾರಾಯಣರು ಎಂದು ಎಚ್ಚರಿಸಿ ಸಂಧಿ ಮಾಡೆಂದು ದುರ್ಯೋಧನನನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಾಯಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: परशुराम राजा दम्भोद्भव की कथा सुनाते हैं, जिसने अहंकार में युद्ध के लिए बराबर का प्रतिद्वन्द्वी खोजा और उसे ऋषि नर और नारायण के पास भेजा गया। नर ने कुशा के तिनकों से उसकी पूरी सेना को हरा दिया, और विनम्र हुए राजा ने ब्राह्मणों का सम्मान करना सीखा; परशुराम चेताते हैं कि अर्जुन और श्रीकृष्ण ही नर और नारायण हैं, और दुर्योधन से सन्धि का आग्रह करते हैं।
summary.te: గర్వంతో యుద్ధంలో సమానుని వెతికి నరనారాయణ ఋషుల దగ్గరకు పంపబడిన దంభోద్భవ రాజు కథను పరశురాముడు చెబుతాడు. నరుడు దర్భ పరకలతోనే అతని సైన్యమంతటినీ ఓడించాడు, వినయం పొందిన రాజు బ్రాహ్మణులను గౌరవించడం నేర్చుకున్నాడు; అర్జునుడు, శ్రీకృష్ణుడే నరనారాయణులని హెచ్చరించి సంధి చేయమని దుర్యోధనుని కోరతాడు.
summary.ta: செருக்கால் போரில் நிகரானவனைத் தேடி நர நாராயண முனிவர்களிடம் அனுப்பப்பட்ட தம்போத்பவ மன்னனின் கதையைப் பரஶுராமர் சொல்கிறார். நரன் தர்ப்பைப் புற்களாலேயே அவன் படை முழுவதையும் வென்றான், பணிவுற்ற மன்னன் அந்தணர்களைப் போற்றக் கற்றான்; அர்ஜுனனும் ஸ்ரீகிருஷ்ணரும் நர நாராயணர்களே என்று எச்சரித்து, சமாதானம் செய்யுமாறு துரியோதனனை வற்புறுத்துகிறார்.
summary.ml: ദംഭോദ്ഭവൻ എന്ന രാജാവ്, അഹങ്കാരത്താൽ യുദ്ധത്തിൽ തനിക്കു തുല്യനെ തേടി, നര-നാരായണ മുനിമാരുടെ അടുത്തേക്ക് നയിക്കപ്പെട്ട കഥ പരശുരാമൻ പറയുന്നു. പുൽനാമ്പുകൾകൊണ്ട് നരൻ അദ്ദേഹത്തിന്റെ മുഴുവൻ സേനയെയും തോൽപ്പിച്ചു; വിനീതനായ രാജാവ് ബ്രാഹ്മണരെ ആദരിക്കാൻ പഠിച്ചു. അർജുനനും കൃഷ്ണനും നരനും നാരായണനുമാണെന്ന് പരശുരാമൻ മുന്നറിയിപ്പ് നൽകുകയും, ദുര്യോധനനോട് സമാധാനമുണ്ടാക്കാൻ അപേക്ഷിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 5.94; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Tue Jan 23 2024

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
तस्मिन्नभिहिते वाक्ये केशवेन महात्मना ।
स्तिमिता हृष्टरोमाण आसन्सर्वे सभासदः ॥

meaning.en: When great-souled Keshava had spoken, all the members of the assembly were stilled, their hair standing on end.

verses.text:
कः स्विदुत्तरमेतस्माद्वक्तुमुत्सहते पुमान् ।
इति सर्वे मनोभिस्ते चिन्तयन्ति स्म पार्थिवाः ॥

meaning.en: Who could dare to answer this? So all those kings thought in their minds.

verses.text:
तथा तेषु च सर्वेषु तूष्णींभूतेषु राजसु ।
जामदग्न्य इदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्कुरुसंसदि ॥

meaning.en: When all the kings had thus fallen silent, Jamadagni's son Parashurama spoke these words in the Kuru assembly.

verses.text:
इमामेकोपमां राजञ्शृणु सत्यामशङ्कितः ।
तां श्रुत्वा श्रेय आदत्स्व यदि साध्विति मन्यसे ॥

meaning.en: King, hear without doubt this one true example; having heard it, take what is best, if you think it good.

verses.text:
राजा दम्भोद्भवो नाम सार्वभौमः पुराभवत् ।
अखिलां बुभुजे सर्वां पृथिवीमिति नः श्रुतम् ॥

meaning.en: Long ago there was a king named Dambhodbhava, an emperor; we have heard that he ruled the whole earth entire.

verses.text:
स स्म नित्यं निशापाये प्रातरुत्थाय वीर्यवान् ।
ब्राह्मणान्क्षत्रियांश्चैव पृच्छन्नास्ते महारथः ॥

meaning.en: That mighty man, rising each morning at night's end, would ask brahmanas and kshatriyas, as the great chariot-warrior,

verses.text:
अस्ति कश्चिद्विशिष्टो वा मद्विधो वा भवेद्युधि ।
शूद्रो वैश्यः क्षत्रियो वा ब्राह्मणो वापि शस्त्रभृत् ॥

meaning.en: Is there anyone better than I, or equal to me in battle, whether shudra, vaishya, kshatriya or a brahmana bearing arms?

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवन्नन्वचरत्स राजा पृथिवीमिमाम् ।
दर्पेण महता मत्तः कंचिदन्यमचिन्तयन् ॥

meaning.en: Saying this he roamed over this earth, drunk with great pride, thinking of no one else.

verses.text:
तं स्म वैद्या अकृपणा ब्राह्मणाः सर्वतोऽभयाः ।
प्रत्यषेधन्त राजानं श्लाघमानं पुनः पुनः ॥

meaning.en: Brahmanas, physicians, unwretched and fearless everywhere, repeatedly forbade the king as he boasted.

verses.text:
प्रतिषिध्यमानोऽप्यसकृत्पृच्छत्येव स वै द्विजान् ।
अभिमानी श्रिया मत्तस्तमूचुर्ब्राह्मणास्तदा ॥

meaning.en: Though forbidden, he kept asking the twice-born again and again, proud and drunk with prosperity; then the brahmanas answered him.

verses.text:
तपस्विनो महात्मानो वेदव्रतसमन्विताः ।
उदीर्यमाणं राजानं क्रोधदीप्ता द्विजातयः ॥

meaning.en: The ascetic great souls, twice-born, observing Vedic vows, burning with anger at the king's boasting, said:

verses.text:
अनेकजननं सख्यं ययोः पुरुषसिंहयोः ।
तयोस्त्वं न समो राजन्भवितासि कदाचन ॥

meaning.en: There are two lions among men whose friendship has lasted through many births; you will never be equal to those two, king.

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः स राजा तु पुनः पप्रच्छ तान्द्विजान् ।
क्व तौ वीरौ क्वजन्मानौ किंकर्माणौ च कौ च तौ ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed, the king again asked those brahmanas: Where are those two heroes, where born, what do they do, and who are they?

verses.text: ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः

meaning.en: The brahmanas said:

verses.text:
नरो नारायणश्चैव तापसाविति नः श्रुतम् ।
आयातौ मानुषे लोके ताभ्यां युध्यस्व पार्थिव ॥

meaning.en: We have heard they are the ascetics Nara and Narayana; they have come to the human world. Fight with them, king.

verses.text:
श्रूयते तौ महात्मानौ नरनारायणावुभौ ।
तपो घोरमनिर्देश्यं तप्येते गन्धमादने ॥

meaning.en: It is heard that those two great souls, Nara and Narayana, practice fearful and indescribable austerity on Gandhamadana.

verses.text: राम उवाच

meaning.en: Rama said:

verses.text:
स राजा महतीं सेनां योजयित्वा षडङ्गिनीम् ।
अमृष्यमाणः संप्रायाद्यत्र तावपराजितौ ॥

meaning.en: That king, unable to bear it, gathered a great army of six divisions and set out where those two unconquered ones were.

verses.text:
स गत्वा विषमं घोरं पर्वतं गन्धमादनम् ।
मृगयाणोऽन्वगच्छत्तौ तापसावपराजितौ ॥

meaning.en: He reached the rough, dreadful mountain Gandhamadana, searching, and found the two unconquered ascetics.

verses.text:
तौ दृष्ट्वा क्षुत्पिपासाभ्यां कृशौ धमनिसंततौ ।
शीतवातातपैश्चैव कर्शितौ पुरुषोत्तमौ ।
अभिगम्योपसंगृह्य पर्यपृच्छदनामयम् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing those two best of men, thin with hunger and thirst, their veins showing, and worn by cold, wind and heat, he approached, saluted them and asked after their welfare.

verses.text:
तमर्चित्वा मूलफलैरासनेनोदकेन च ।
न्यमन्त्रयेतां राजानं किं कार्यं क्रियतामिति ॥

meaning.en: They honored him with roots, fruits, a seat and water, and asked the king: What shall be done for you?

verses.text: दम्भोद्भव उवाच

meaning.en: Dambhodbhava said:

verses.text:
बाहुभ्यां मे जिता भूमिर्निहताः सर्वशत्रवः ।
भवद्भ्यां युद्धमाकाङ्क्षन्नुपयातोऽस्मि पर्वतम् ।
आतिथ्यं दीयतामेतत्काङ्क्षितं मे चिरं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: I conquered the earth with my arms and killed all my enemies; wishing for battle with you two I came to this mountain. Grant me this hospitality, which I have long desired.

verses.text: नरनारायणावूचतुः

meaning.en: Nara and Narayana said:

verses.text:
अपेतक्रोधलोभोऽयमाश्रमो राजसत्तम ।
न ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रमे युद्धं कुतः शस्त्रं कुतोऽनृजुः ।
अन्यत्र युद्धमाकाङ्क्ष्व बहवः क्षत्रियाः क्षितौ ॥

meaning.en: Best of kings, this hermitage is free of anger and greed; there is no fighting in this hermitage, so where are weapons or crookedness? Seek battle elsewhere; there are many kshatriyas on earth.

verses.text: राम उवाच

meaning.en: Rama said:

verses.text:
उच्यमानस्तथापि स्म भूय एवाभ्यभाषत ।
पुनः पुनः क्षम्यमाणः सान्त्व्यमानश्च भारत ।
दम्भोद्भवो युद्धमिच्छन्नाह्वयत्येव तापसौ ॥

meaning.en: Though told so, he spoke again, Bharata; pardoned and soothed again and again, Dambhodbhava, longing for battle, kept challenging the two ascetics.

verses.text:
ततो नरस्त्विषीकाणां मुष्टिमादाय कौरव ।
अब्रवीदेहि युध्यस्व युद्धकामुक क्षत्रिय ॥

meaning.en: Then Nara, taking a handful of reeds, said, Kaurava: Come, fight, kshatriya hungry for battle.

verses.text:
सर्वशस्त्राणि चादत्स्व योजयस्व च वाहिनीम् ।
अहं हि ते विनेष्यामि युद्धश्रद्धामितः परम् ॥

meaning.en: Take up all your weapons and array your army; I shall cure you of your craving for battle from now on.

verses.text: दम्भोद्भव उवाच

meaning.en: Dambhodbhava said:

verses.text:
यद्येतदस्त्रमस्मासु युक्तं तापस मन्यसे ।
एतेनापि त्वया योत्स्ये युद्धार्थी ह्यहमागतः ॥

meaning.en: Ascetic, if you think this weapon is suitable against us, I shall fight even with this; for I came wanting battle.

verses.text: राम उवाच

meaning.en: Rama said:

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा शरवर्षेण सर्वतः समवाकिरत् ।
दम्भोद्भवस्तापसं तं जिघांसुः सहसैनिकः ॥

meaning.en: So saying, Dambhodbhava, wishing to kill that ascetic, with his troops showered arrows on him from all sides.

verses.text:
तस्य तानस्यतो घोरानिषून्परतनुच्छिदः ।
कदर्थीकृत्य स मुनिरिषीकाभिरपानुदत् ॥

meaning.en: As the king shot those terrible arrows that pierce enemy bodies, the sage made light of them and warded them off with reeds.

verses.text:
ततोऽस्मै प्रासृजद्घोरमैषीकमपराजितः ।
अस्त्रमप्रतिसंधेयं तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥

meaning.en: Then the unconquered one loosed against him a terrible weapon made of reeds, which could not be countered, and it seemed a wonder.

verses.text:
तेषामक्षीणि कर्णांश्च नस्तकांश्चैव मायया ।
निमित्तवेधी स मुनिरिषीकाभिः समर्पयत् ॥

meaning.en: By his magic that sage, striking where he aimed, pierced their eyes, ears and heads with the reeds.

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा श्वेतमाकाशमिषीकाभिः समाचितम् ।
पादयोर्न्यपतद्राजा स्वस्ति मेऽस्त्विति चाब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the sky white, filled with reeds, the king fell at his feet and said: Let there be peace for me.

verses.text:
तमब्रवीन्नरो राजञ्शरण्यः शरणैषिणाम् ।
ब्रह्मण्यो भव धर्मात्मा मा च स्मैवं पुनः कृथाः ॥

meaning.en: Nara said to him: King, refuge of those seeking refuge, be devoted to brahmanas, be righteous, and do not do this again.

verses.text:
मा च दर्पसमाविष्टः क्षेप्सीः कांश्चित्कदाचन ।
अल्पीयांसं विशिष्टं वा तत्ते राजन्परं हितम् ॥

meaning.en: Never be overcome by pride and scorn anyone, lesser or greater; that is best for you, king.

verses.text:
कृतप्रज्ञो वीतलोभो निरहंकार आत्मवान् ।
दान्तः क्षान्तो मृदुः क्षेमः प्रजाः पालय पार्थिव ॥

meaning.en: Be of settled wisdom, free of greed and egotism, self-possessed, self-controlled, patient and gentle; protect your subjects peacefully, lord of the earth.

verses.text:
अनुज्ञातः स्वस्ति गच्छ मैवं भूयः समाचरेः ।
कुशलं ब्राह्मणान्पृच्छेरावयोर्वचनाद्भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: With our leave, go in peace; do not act so again. And greatly ask after the brahmanas' welfare in our name.

verses.text:
ततो राजा तयोः पादावभिवाद्य महात्मनोः ।
प्रत्याजगाम स्वपुरं धर्मं चैवाचिनोद्भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the king bowed to the feet of the two great souls and returned to his city, and thereafter greatly accumulated merit.

verses.text:
सुमहच्चापि तत्कर्म यन्नरेण कृतं पुरा ।
ततो गुणैः सुबहुभिः श्रेष्ठो नारायणोऽभवत् ॥

meaning.en: And great was that deed done by Nara long ago; yet Narayana is greater still, by his many virtues.

verses.text:
तस्माद्यावद्धनुःश्रेष्ठे गाण्डीवेऽस्त्रं न युज्यते ।
तावत्त्वं मानमुत्सृज्य गच्छ राजन्धनंजयम् ॥

meaning.en: Therefore, king, before the weapon is fitted to Gandiva, the best of bows, give up your pride and go to Dhananjaya.

verses.text:
काकुदीकं शुकं नाकमक्षिसंतर्जनं तथा ।
संतानं नर्तनं घोरमास्यमोदकमष्टमम् ॥

meaning.en: Kakudika, Shuka, Naka, Akshisantarjana, Santana, Nartana, the terrible Asyamodaka as eighth,

verses.text:
एतैर्विद्धाः सर्व एव मरणं यान्ति मानवाः ।
उन्मत्ताश्च विचेष्टन्ते नष्टसंज्ञा विचेतसः ॥

meaning.en: struck by these, all men go to death; they thrash about mad, losing consciousness and sense.

verses.text:
स्वपन्ते च प्लवन्ते च छर्दयन्ति च मानवाः ।
मूत्रयन्ते च सततं रुदन्ति च हसन्ति च ॥

meaning.en: They sleep, float, vomit, constantly urinate, weep and laugh.

verses.text:
असंख्येया गुणाः पार्थे तद्विशिष्टो जनार्दनः ।
त्वमेव भूयो जानासि कुन्तीपुत्रं धनंजयम् ॥

meaning.en: Partha's virtues are beyond counting, and Janardana is greater still; you yourself know more of Kunti's son Dhananjaya.

verses.text:
नरनारायणौ यौ तौ तावेवार्जुनकेशवौ ।
विजानीहि महाराज प्रवीरौ पुरुषर्षभौ ॥

meaning.en: Those who were Nara and Narayana are Arjuna and Keshava; know them, great king, as two foremost heroes, bulls among men.

verses.text:
यद्येतदेवं जानासि न च मामतिशङ्कसे ।
आर्यां मतिं समास्थाय शाम्य भारत पाण्डवैः ॥

meaning.en: If you know this and do not doubt me, take the noble course, Bharata, and make peace with the Pandavas.

verses.text:
अथ चेन्मन्यसे श्रेयो न मे भेदो भवेदिति ।
प्रशाम्य भरतश्रेष्ठ मा च युद्धे मनः कृथाः ॥

meaning.en: And if you think it best that there be no split between us, calm yourself, best of the Bharatas, and do not set your mind on war.

verses.text:
भवतां च कुरुश्रेष्ठ कुलं बहुमतं भुवि ।
तत्तथैवास्तु भद्रं ते स्वार्थमेवानुचिन्तय ॥

meaning.en: Your family, best of the Kurus, is highly esteemed on earth; let it be so; good fortune to you; think of your own interest.
